title: vLLM x AgentX: optimizing for real-world agentic serving
gist: The general-purpose open engine reworked for agent traffic: a shared KV block pool, cache retention aware of sessions, a cap on long prefills in the scheduler, and per-model parallelism choices. On this workload, simply keeping a session on the same server beat every load-balancing signal.
changes: The workload class changed the engine's design, not only its settings. And because it happened in the commons, everyone got it.
caveats: No before-optimisation baseline for the headline throughput. The prefill cap buys throughput by making long requests wait longer for a first token. Hints from the agent harness are future work.

numbers.metric: Total tokens per GPU-second from a 512-token cap on long prefills
numbers.baseline: the same engine without the cap

numbers.metric: Prefill with context parallelism on a 32K prompt

bears_on.note: Agent sessions (median 43 turns, 142K input tokens, 96% prefix hits) needed different scheduling and caching from chat.
Changes for the whole class, in the shared engine, delivered the bulk of the gain with no per-customer work.
